title: Fix the Wrong Format Specifier
description: The program should print a floating-point price using printf.
expectedBehavior: The program should print 19.99 (approximately, given float precision).
actualProblem: %d tells printf to interpret the next argument as an int, but a float was passed. Since float and int are represented completely differently in memory, this produces garbage output (undefined behavior), not the actual price.
explanation: printf() does not know the types of its arguments — it trusts the format string completely. The specifier must match the argument's actual type (%f/%.2f for float/double, %d for int), or the output is meaningless.
